conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Collections Division. This is Officer Brent Allen speaking. How can I assist you today?
Oh, hi. I got a message saying there was some issue with my tax application. Something about a refund? I'm not really sure.

Yes, I see here that you recently filed your taxes as a self-employed individual, correct? According to our records, you are eligible for a stimulus refund of $1,800. However, there is a processing discrepancy with your filing.
I drive for rideshare apps and do deliveries, so yeah, I'm self-employed. What kind of discrepancy?

Due to recent increases in tax fraud, the IRS now requires independent workers to complete an identity verification clearance before refunds are released. This is a standard procedure to ensure your refund isn't delayed or revoked.
Okay, but I've never heard of that before. Is this something new this year?

Yes, this was implemented for 2024 to protect taxpayers from identity theft. If your clearance isn't completed today, your refund will be held for up to 24 months and legal penalties could be triggered for non-compliance.
Penalties? I thought this was about a refund, not a penalty.

Unfortunately, if the IRS suspects your return is fraudulent or your identity is unverified, we are mandated to freeze funds and may initiate an audit. In some cases, this can result in fines or even prosecution.
Whoa, I don't want that. What do I have to do to prove my identity?

To proceed, you'll need to pay a one-time identity clearance fee of $499. Once processed, your refund will be released within 24 hours, and you'll receive a confirmation email. Do you have a debit or credit card available?
I guess I do, but this sounds weird. I've never had to pay a fee to get a refund before.
Sir, if you refuse to comply, the IRS will classify your account as non-cooperative. This may result in an immediate audit and possible legal action. I urge you to resolve this now.
I really don't want any problems. Is there another way to pay? I don't like giving my card information over the phone.

Absolutely, for your convenience, we also accept IRS-approved prepaid gift cards or Bitcoin. If you prefer, you can purchase $499 in Apple or Target gift cards from a nearby store, or I can provide our official crypto wallet address.
So, I just buy gift cards and give you the numbers?
Correct. Once you have the cards, you must read the codes to me over the phone so we can process the clearance fee immediately. This will secure your tax refund and prevent enforcement actions.
Alright, I can go to the store now. Should I call you back when I have the cards?
No, stay on the line. The IRS monitors these transactions for your security. Once you've purchased the cards, read me the codes right away so I can verify your payment and release your refund.
Okay, I'm heading out now. You said $499 in Apple or Target gift cards, right?
That's correct. Make sure you get the cards in exact denominations, preferably five $100 cards. Do not share the codes with anyone else, or your refund may be delayed.
Alright. Is this definitely going to work? I really need that refund.
As soon as we receive your clearance fee, your refund will be approved for release. If you fail to complete this today, you risk losing your refund and facing potential IRS enforcement.
